verifications.claim: Artemis III is currently targeted for launch in mid-2027, according to NASA.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Launch Schedule Artemis III When 2027'; R2: 'NASA's next mission... slated to launch sometime in 2027'; R3: 'it will be launched by mid-2027'
verifications.reasoning: NASA sources (R1) and reports (R2, R3) directly support 2027 target, with R3 specifying mid-2027 from NASA announcement.

verifications.claim: Artemis III will be a crewed mission aimed at testing rendezvous and docking capabilities with commercial landers in low-Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA's Artemis III demonstration mission in low Earth orbit... test rendezvous and docking capabilities between Orion and private commercial spacecraft'; R5: 'Artemis III mission in low Earth orbit will test... rendezvous and docking capabilities'; R3: 'low-Earth orbit designed to test essential technologies'
verifications.reasoning: Direct descriptions in NASA sources match crewed LEO rendezvous/docking test with commercial landers.

verifications.claim: As of April 2026, Artemis III launch date is scheduled for 2027.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2 (dated April 10, 2026): 'Artemis III launch date... slated to launch sometime in 2027'
verifications.reasoning: Article from April 2026 explicitly states 2027 schedule.

verifications.claim: Space.com reported that the Artemis III crew will launch on the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket in the Orion spacecraft.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No cited reference is from Space.com or mentions Space.com reporting this; content appears in R1/R5 but attribution to Space.com unsupported.

verifications.claim: Space.com reported that the Artemis III crew will dock with a commercial lander (such as SpaceX’s Starship) in low-Earth orbit, rather than immediately landing on the Moon.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No cited reference is from Space.com or mentions Space.com reporting this; content appears in R1/R3/R5 but attribution to Space.com unsupported.

verifications.claim: SpaceNews and The Guardian note that the Artemis III mission revision follows concerns over technological readiness, focusing on addressing delays in the human landing system (HLS).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3 (Guardian): 'radical changes... grapples with technical glitches... delays and technical problems... aerospace safety advisory panel... too risky'; R4 (SpaceNews): 'changing the scope of Artemis 3... if key elements suffer major delays... concern about... SpaceX... Starship... lunar lander'
verifications.reasoning: Both sources attribute revisions to tech delays/readiness issues, with R4 specifically on HLS (Starship).

verifications.claim: The actual human lunar landing has been shifted to the Artemis IV mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'The Artemis III mission will no longer aim to land on the moon... a new Artemis IV mission would set out in 2028 to land on the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Directly states shift of landing from III to IV.

verifications.claim: Artemis IV mission is now targeted for 2028.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'a new Artemis IV mission would set out in 2028 to land on the moon'
